record.paper_title: Open problems on regular languages: an historical perspective
record.context_brief: Largest proper lp-variety closed under shuffle
record.original_question: Consider lp-varieties of languages, meaning classes of recognizable languages that satisfy the variety closure conditions with inverse morphisms restricted to length-preserving morphisms. Is there a largest proper lp-variety of languages that is closed under the shuffle product?

evidence.quote:
It would be interesting to know whether a similar result holds for lp￾varieties of languages: is there a largest proper lp-variety of languages closed
under shuffle?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and let $A^*$ denote the free monoid on $A$. A language $L \subseteq A^*$ is recognizable if it is recognized by a finite monoid. A morphism $\varphi: A^* \to B^*$ between free monoids is length-preserving (lp) if $|\varphi(a)| = 1$ for every $a \in A$, i.e., $\varphi$ sends each letter to a letter.

An lp-variety of languages is an operator $\mathcal{V}$ that assigns to every finite alphabet $A$ a class $\mathcal{V}(A^*)$ of recognizable languages of $A^*$ such that:
(i) $\mathcal{V}(A^*)$ is a Boolean algebra (closed under finite union, finite intersection, and complement);
(ii) $\mathcal{V}(A^*)$ is closed under left and right quotients by words: if $L \in \mathcal{V}(A^*)$ and $u \in A^*$, then $u^{-1}L = \{v \in A^* : uv \in L\} \in \mathcal{V}(A^*)$ and $Lu^{-1} = \{v \in A^* : vu \in L\} \in \mathcal{V}(A^*)$;
(iii) for every length-preserving morphism $\varphi: A^* \to B^*$ and every $L \in \mathcal{V}(B^*)$, one has $\varphi^{-1}(L) \in \mathcal{V}(A^*)$.

An lp-variety $\mathcal{V}$ is called proper if there exist a finite alphabet $A$ and a recognizable language $L \subseteq A^*$ with $L \notin \mathcal{V}(A^*)$.

The shuffle product of two languages $K, L \subseteq A^*$ is
$$K \shuffle L = \{u_1 v_1 u_2 v_2 \cdots u_n v_n : n \geq 1,\ u_i, v_i \in A^*,\ u_1 u_2 \cdots u_n \in K,\ v_1 v_2 \cdots v_n \in L\}.$$
An lp-variety $\mathcal{V}$ is closed under shuffle if for every finite alphabet $A$ and every $K, L \in \mathcal{V}(A^*)$, also $K \shuffle L \in \mathcal{V}(A^*)$.

Question: Does there exist a largest proper lp-variety of languages that is closed under the shuffle product? That is, does there exist a proper lp-variety $\mathcal{W}$ closed under shuffle such that every proper lp-variety closed under shuffle is contained in $\mathcal{W}$?
artifact.status_search_result: For positive varieties, it is known (Ésik–Simon, 1998, confirming a conjecture of Perrot) that there is a largest proper positive variety closed under shuffle, namely the positive variety not containing $(ab)^*$. The analogous question for lp-varieties (where inverse morphism closure is restricted to length-preserving morphisms) appears to still be posed as an open problem, with no resolution found in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Shuffle on positive varieties of languages
status_evidence.snippet: There is a largest proper positive variety W closed under shuffle, characterized algebraically; W is the largest positive variety not containing (ab)*.
status_evidence.claim: The analogous theorem for positive varieties is known (Ésik–Simon), but the lp-variety version is posed as a separate open question.

status_evidence.title: Shuffle product of regular languages: results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on shuffle closure for various types of varieties of languages.
status_evidence.claim: The lp-variety analog is included among open problems on shuffle in the survey literature.
